That simple idea became one of the most influential RL algorithms. Powering work in robotics, games, RLHF, and MARL.
It is battle tested and will not die anytime soon. It has become a game changer for devices with low computational power to train reasonable agents.

TRPO: “Let’s mathematically constrain policy updates.”
PPO: "What if we just, clip the ratio?"

check each bin's cleanliness, see how far it is from an 80% passing grade, average all 4 bins, make the number louder, then squish it into a safe range between -1 and +1. That final squished number is the reward the sort agent gets that step.

- 2.0/0.5 is there to amplify (x4) the performance difference, so that bad performance feels a lot worse and good performance feels a lot better.
- tanh function is used to put a ceiling and floor between -1 to +1 on it. Important to prevent extreme reward or punishment values.

- 'pₘ' represents purity of a container m and an empty container counts as 0.9 purity.
- 'θ' represents passing grade for purity and is set to 0.8.
- 1/4 ∑ is there to average all 4 bins together.
Calculation of sorting agent's reward provision.
